$comment: The dependency list, in one place, pinned.
This used to be a `vcpkg install ffmpeg[...]` line in README.md that every
machine ran by hand into a shared classic-mode tree, which meant the set of
libraries this application links was whatever each machine happened to have
installed on the day it last read that line. A manifest is the same list as a
fact the build reads: with the vcpkg toolchain active these install into
<build>/vcpkg_installed at configure time, and `builtin-baseline` pins every
port and every transitive (openssl, protobuf, harfbuzz, ...) to the versions at
that microsoft/vcpkg commit, so a local build and a CI build link the same
libraries at the same versions.
The baseline is the same commit bro's own vcpkg.json pins, deliberately: bro is
added with add_subdirectory here, so its services are configured against these
ports rather than against its own manifest, which vcpkg never reads (only the
top-level one counts). Two baselines would be two answers to the question of
which protobuf bro links. The workflows clone vcpkg at this same commit, so
keep VCPKG_COMMIT in .github/workflows/*.yml in step when bumping it.
ffmpeg is listed twice on purpose. vcpkg merges the feature sets, and the
second entry carries the two vendor accelerations that do not exist on Apple
hardware: `nvcodec` is `supports: linux | (!osx & ...)` and `amf` pulls
amd-amf, which is `supports: !osx`. Qualifying them is what lets one manifest
serve all three platforms instead of macOS failing to resolve.
`default-features: false` is the manifest spelling of the `core` that leads a
classic-mode bracket list, because ffmpeg's defaults drag in ports nothing here
asks for. `gpl` and `version3` are what x264 and x265 require, and are the
whole reason this binary is GPL-3.0-or-later; see LICENSE.
The last five are bro's, copied from bro/vcpkg.json rather than inherited,
because a nested manifest is not read. If bro's list changes, this one has to.
name: ffmpeg-bro
